arxiv-2109-01738.title: A look at endemic equilibria of compartmental epidemiological models and model control via vaccination and mitigation
arxiv-2109-01738.creator: Monique Chyba, Taylor Klotz, Yuriy Mileyko, Corey Shanbrom
arxiv-2109-01738.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Monique Chyba, Taylor Klotz, Yuriy Mileyko, Corey Shanbrom. Compartmental models have long served as important tools in mathematical epidemiology, with their usefulness highlighted by the recent COVID-19 pandemic. However, most of the classical models fail to account for certain features of this disease and others like it, such as the ability of exposed individuals to recover without becoming infectious, or the possibility that asymptomatic individuals can indeed transmit the disease but at a lesser rate than the symptomatic.

Cas
arxiv-2206-10048.description: Abstract In the medical field, multi-center collaborations are often sought to yield more generalizable findings by leveraging the heterogeneity of patient and clinical data. However, recent privacy regulations hinder the possibility to share data, and consequently, to come up with machine learning-based solutions that support diagnosis and prognosis.

arxiv-2209-06295.title: Data-adaptive Transfer Learning for Translation: A Case Study in Haitian and Jamaican
arxiv-2209-06295.creator: Nathaniel R. Robinson, Cameron J. Hogan, Nancy Fulda, David R. Mortensen
arxiv-2209-06295.description: Abstract Multilingual transfer techniques often improve low-resource machine translation (MT). Many of these techniques are applied without considering data characteristics. We show in the context of Haitian-to-English translation that transfer effectiveness is correlated with amount of training data and relationships between knowledge-sharing languages.

arxiv-2209-15314.title: Did You Get What You Paid For? Rethinking Annotation Cost of Deep Learning Based Computer Aided Detection in Chest Radiographs
arxiv-2209-15314.creator: Tae Soo Kim, Geonwoon Jang ∗, Sanghyup Lee, Thijs Kooi
arxiv-2209-15314.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Tae Soo Kim, Geonwoon Jang ∗, Sanghyup Lee, Thijs Kooi. As deep networks require large amounts of accurately labeled training data, a strategy to collect sufficiently large and accurate annotations is as important as innovations in recognition methods. This is especially true for building Computer Aided Detection (CAD) systems for chest X-rays where domain expertise of radiologists is required to annotate the presence and location of abnormalities on X-ray images.

arxiv-2301-11881.title: Electromagnetic Form Factors and Charge Radii of Pseudoscalar and Scalar Mesons: A Comprehensive Contact Interaction Analysis
arxiv-2301-11881.creator: R. J. Hernández-Pinto, L. X. Gutiérrez-Guerrero, A. Bashir, M. A. Bedolla, I. M. Higuera-Angulo
arxiv-2301-11881.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by R. J. Hernández-Pinto, L. X. Gutiérrez-Guerrero, A. Bashir, M. A. Bedolla, I. M. Higuera-Angulo. We carry out a comprehensive survey of electromagnetic form factors of all light, heavy and heavy-light ground-state pseudoscalar and scalar mesons. Our analysis is based upon a Schwinger-Dyson equations treatment of a vector × \times vector contact interaction. It incorporates confinement and ensures axial vector and vector Ward-Takahashi identities are satisfied along with the corresponding corollaries such as the Goldberger-Treiman relations.

arxiv-2311-05601.title: FAMuS: Frames Across Multiple Sources
arxiv-2311-05601.creator: Siddharth Vashishtha 1 Alexander Martin 1 William Gantt 1
arxiv-2311-05601.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Siddharth Vashishtha 1 Alexander Martin 1 William Gantt 1. Understanding event descriptions is a central aspect of language processing, but current approaches focus overwhelmingly on single sentences or documents. Aggregating information about an event across documents can offer a much richer understanding. To this end, we present FAMuS, a new corpus of Wikipedia passages that report on some event, paired with underlying, genre-diverse (non-Wikipedia) source articles for the same event.

arxiv-2312-00313.title: Improving Normalization with the James-Stein Estimator
arxiv-2312-00313.creator: Seyedalireza Khoshsirat, Chandra Kambhamettu
arxiv-2312-00313.description: Abstract Stein’s paradox holds considerable sway in high-dimensional statistics, highlighting that the sample mean, traditionally considered the de facto estimator, might not be the most efficacious in higher dimensions. To address this, the James-Stein estimator proposes an enhancement by steering the sample means toward a more centralized mean vector.

arxiv-2312-14976.title: Gaussian Harmony: Attaining Fairness in Diffusion-based Face Generation Models
arxiv-2312-14976.creator: Basudha Pal, Arunkumar Kannan, Ram Prabhakar Kathirvel, Alice J. O’Toole, Rama Chellappa
arxiv-2312-14976.description: Abstract Diffusion models have achieved great progress in face generation. However, these models amplify the bias in the generation process, leading to an imbalance in distribution of sensitive attributes such as age, gender and race. This paper proposes a novel solution to this problem by balancing the facial attributes of the generated images.

arxiv-2402-01769.title: Redefining ”Hallucination” in LLMs: Towards a psychology-informed framework for mitigating misinformation
arxiv-2402-01769.creator: Elijah Berberette, Jack Hutchins, Amir Sadovnik
arxiv-2402-01769.description: Abstract In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have become incredibly popular, with ChatGPT for example being used by over a billion users. While these models exhibit remarkable language understanding and logical prowess, a notable challenge surfaces in the form of ”hallucinations.

arxiv-2409-01883.title: Boosting Vision-Language Models for Histopathology Classification: Predict all at once
arxiv-2409-01883.creator: Maxime Zanella, Fereshteh Shakeri ∗, Yunshi Huang, Houda Bahig, Ismail Ben Ayed
arxiv-2409-01883.description: Abstract The development of vision-language models (VLMs) for histo-pathology has shown promising new usages and zero-shot performances. However, current approaches, which decompose large slides into smaller patches, focus solely on inductive classification, i.e., prediction for each patch is made independently of the other patches in the target test data.

arxiv-2410-02332.title: Polynomial time constructive decision algorithm for multivariable quantum signal processing
arxiv-2410-02332.creator: Yuki Ito, Hitomi Mori, Kazuki Sakamoto, Keisuke Fujii
arxiv-2410-02332.description: Abstract Quantum signal processing (QSP) and quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) have provided a unified framework for understanding many quantum algorithms, including factorization, matrix inversion, and Hamiltonian simulation. As a multivariable version of QSP, multivariable quantum signal processing (M-QSP) is proposed.

arxiv-2505-22283.title: Intermittency in Interplanetary Coronal Mass Ejections Observed by Parker Solar Probe and Solar Orbiter
arxiv-2505-22283.creator: Julia Ruohotie, Simon Good, Christian Möstl, Emilia Kilpua
arxiv-2505-22283.description: Abstract Intermittency has been studied extensively in the fast and slow solar winds but to a far lesser extent in interplanetary coronal mass ejections (ICMEs). While ICMEs are often characterized by their relatively smooth, large-scale magnetic flux rope structures, a spectrum of fluctuations is nonetheless present at smaller scales.

arxiv-2508-05270.title: Commuting integrable maps from a deformed D 4 cluster algebra
arxiv-2508-05270.creator: Andrew N. W. Hone, Wookyung Kim, Takafumi Mase
arxiv-2508-05270.description: Abstract A cluster algebra is a special type of commutative algebra whose generators are defined iteratively from an initial seed via a process called mutation. The simplest cluster algebras are those of finite type, whose seeds are classified (up to mutations) by Dynkin diagrams of simple Lie algebras.

pmc-11431196.title: Neurobiological Implications of Chronic Stress and Metabolic Dysregulation in Inflammatory Bowel Diseases
pmc-11431196.creator: Aleksandar Sic, Kiana Cvetkovic, Eshanika Manchanda, Nebojsa Nick Knezevic, Arrigo Cicero
pmc-11431196.description: Chronic stress is a significant factor affecting modern society, with profound implications for both physical and mental health. Central to the stress response is cortisol, a glucocorticoid hormone produced by the adrenal glands. While cortisol release is adaptive in acute stress, prolonged exposure to elevated levels can result in adverse effects.

pmc-11582210.title: Changes in MRI head motion across development: typical development and ADHD
pmc-11582210.creator: Phoebe Thomson, Vanessa Loosley, Emily Friedel, Timothy J Silk
pmc-11582210.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Head motion is a major confounding variable for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) analysis, and is commonly seen in individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders such as attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). This study investigated the trajectory of change in head motion in typically developing children and children with ADHD, and examined possible altered trajectories in head motion between children with remitted and persistent ADHD.
